title: Lesson 20: Simple Repeatable Workflows You Can Run Weekly
description: What turns a prompt into a workflow, the check step that never gets skipped, and why a fixed time budget keeps a routine running.

questions.question: What turns a single prompt into a workflow?
options: Running the same prompt more than once
A fixed sequence of steps, run in order, that feeds a recurring result
Saving the prompt somewhere you can find it again
questions.explanation: A prompt is one request, while a workflow is several steps arranged so each one hands its output to the next. The order and the handoffs are what make it a routine.

questions.question: What is the role of the final check in a workflow?
options: It speeds up the drafting steps
It replaces the need for saved prompts
It is where you verify the output before it leaves your hands
It only runs until the workflow proves stable, then stops
questions.explanation: The check is where the human decides, and it is the step never skipped. A routine that ships output nobody verified is delegation, not a safe workflow.

questions.question: Why should a weekly workflow get a fixed time budget?
options: A routine you can finish in a set window actually runs every week, while one that sprawls gets skipped
It makes the tool's output more accurate
It stops the tool from running for too long
It is how the subscription is billed
questions.explanation: A workflow is a habit, and habits survive when they stay small. A set window keeps it bounded enough to run every week instead of ballooning into a task you keep skipping.
